notes: HONESTY SUMMARY: the 17 EN 206 Table F.1 rows are 'typical' = recalled from the standard (handbook-level, widely reproduced), NOT confirmed tonight. Literature MCPs (SciSpace, Consensus, FastTrack) return abstracts only and none reproduced the table; pages that do reproduce it (umwelt-online.de, de.wikipedia.org, heidelbergmaterials.de, EC TRIS) are blocked by this session's network settings, so two-source confirmation was not possible. Seen tonight: XF4 w/c 0.45 + 340 kg/m3 (Smets 2024, 1 source); XM1-XM3 limits (web-search summary of Heidelberg Materials poster, 1 source); wording for XS1/XS2/XS3; partial corroboration for XC4 (300 kg/m3) and XD3 (C35/45). See field_evidence per row. Sourced context: Ribeiro et al. 2003: 'Annex F of European Standard EN 206-1 gives recommendations for limiting values of concrete composition. These values are based on the assumption of an intended structural service life of 50 years.' (https://scispace.com/papers/performance-of-concrete-with-an-intended-working-life-of-50-4sj8wkt3q1) - so do not scale these limits to 100 years without labelling. Table F.1 is informative and assumes CEM I; national annexes differ (search output tonight showed Irish and Swiss tables with other cement contents; DIN 1045-2 is generally less strict for XC1-XC4). min_cylinder_strength_MPa is the first number of the class name (Cx/y = cylinder/cube characteristic strength, by definition). min_air_content_pct 4.0 for XF2-XF4 is typical (alternative: prove performance by freeze-thaw test); XF aggregates need freeze-thaw resistance per EN 12620; XA2/XA3 need sulfate-resisting cement when sulfate is the attack (typical). X0 (no risk, C12/15, no w/c or cement limit) omitted. Label suggestion for the app: 'EN 206 Table F.1 recommended values (informative, 50-year design life); not verified against the standard text'.
